gloss: parent bird; adult bird; old hen (in cooking)

definitions.explanation: A bird that has offspring, or an adult bird as opposed to a chick. Used when discussing bird behavior, especially nesting and feeding.
In cooking, a fully grown, older chicken as opposed to a young one ({若鶏|わかどり}). The meat is tougher but more flavorful.

examples.japanese: {親鳥|おやどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ヒナ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{餌|えさ}→餌：01886_esa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{運|はこ}んでいる→運ぶ：01088_hakobu⟧。
examples.english: The parent bird is bringing food to the chick.
If you go near the nest, the parent bird will act aggressively.

examples.japanese: {親鳥|おやどり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{巣|す}→巣：02140_su⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{餌場|えさば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{往復|おうふく}→往復：04111_oufuku⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、ヒナ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{育|そだ}てる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧。
examples.english: The parent bird raises its chicks by going back and forth between the nest and the feeding ground many times.
Old hen meat is tough but rich in flavor.

examples.english: Unlike young chicken, old hen has a chewy texture, so it is suitable for stewed dishes.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧ (parent) and {鳥|どり} (bird), with rendaku on ⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧. The two senses are used in quite different contexts: sense 1 in nature observation and biology, sense 2 in cooking and food. In some regions of Japan, particularly in Kagawa Prefecture's {骨付鳥|ほねつきどり}, the distinction between {親鳥|おやどり} and {若鳥|わかどり} is an important menu choice.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {親鳥|おやどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{巣|す}→巣：02140_su⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧: the parent bird protects the nest
- {親鳥|おやどり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{餌|えさ}→餌：01886_esa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}える→与える：01821_ataeru⟧: the parent bird feeds (its young)
- {親鳥|おやどり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧: old hen meat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {若鶏|わかどり}: young chicken — tender, commonly used in cooking
- ヒナ: chick; baby bird — the offspring that the {親鳥|おやどり} raises
- ⟦{雛鳥|ひなどり}→雛鳥：24779_hinadori⟧: fledgling; young bird — a slightly more formal term for a baby bird
